clue.text: Fighting vessel from Kent

definitions.meaning: a small armed warship of the sailing navy, carrying guns on one deck
a novel by Alexander Kent, one of his Richard Bolitho naval adventures

explanation.surface: A warship launched from a port in the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent here is not the English county but the naval novelist Alexander Kent, whose Bolitho series includes a book of this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the same thing: the historic small warship and the novel titled after that kind of ship.

clue.text: South American exercises for Ruritanian officer

parts.note: PT, physical training, is drill or exercises

explanation.surface: A soldier from South America does his drills before joining a foreign army.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruritania is the imaginary kingdom of Anthony Hope's The Prisoner of Zenda, where Colonel Sapt serves the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Sapt is the loyal soldier who guards the king in Hope's novel set in that invented kingdom.

clue.text: Old coin still carries weight in Greece

definitions.meaning: a small silver piece of ancient Greek money
it was also a small ancient Greek unit of weight

explanation.surface: An ancient coin is still a weighty matter in modern Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek term served both as a small silver currency piece and as a measure of mass.

clue.text: Lamia's Orphic new version betrays narrow outlook

indicators.note: a new version of these words means their letters are recast into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh rendering of an Orphic poem about Lamia shows a blinkered view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new version' rearranges the twelve letters of LAMIAS ORPHIC; 'betrays' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish-pump attitude is one confined to local concerns and blind to the wider world.

clue.text: Poetical Roman calendar also gives note on Italian wine

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: F is a musical note
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy

explanation.surface: A Roman almanac in verse also offers tasting notes on an Italian wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fasti is Ovid's poem on the Roman calendar; 'also gives' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid wrote a verse work on the Roman year and its festivals under this Latin title, meaning the calendar of days.

clue.text: Eminence inspiring Milton's attack on censorship

definitions.text: Eminence inspiring Milton's attack on censorship

parts.words: Eminence inspiring Milton's attack on censorship
parts.note: Milton's pamphlet against licensing of the press, Areopagitica, took its name from a hill in Athens where a council sat

explanation.surface: A great figure who moved Milton to write against censorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' suggests an important person, but here it is literally a hill: the Athenian rock that named Milton's Areopagitica.
explanation.definitionFit: The rocky hill in Athens, seat of an ancient court, gave its name to Milton's famous plea for a free press.

clue.text: A cunning hunter, and hairy with it

definitions.text: A cunning hunter, and hairy with it

parts.words: A cunning hunter, and hairy with it
parts.note: Genesis describes Jacob's brother as a skilful hunter and a hairy man

explanation.surface: A crafty huntsman who is also rather shaggy.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis 25:27 calls Isaac's elder son 'a cunning hunter', and 27:11 'a hairy man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names Jacob's twin brother as both the skilled huntsman and the hairy one.

clue.text: Medieval glossographers lash stoics indiscriminately

indicators.note: mixing things indiscriminately means jumbling the letters of lash stoics without order

explanation.surface: Medieval commentators whip philosophers of the Stoic school without discrimination.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient and medieval commentators wrote explanatory notes in manuscript margins, which is what glossographers did.

clue.text: A Hindu pass conceals sacred books

indicators.note: conceals suggests the words a Hindu pass disguise the answer's letters in a scrambled order

explanation.surface: A Hindu mountain pass hides a store of holy texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' looks like a hidden-word signal, but no run of consecutive letters works: all ten letters of A HINDU PASS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosophical scriptures of ancient India, appended to the Vedas, are the holy writings meant.

clue.text: Villainous Greek pores hopelessly over meagre ration

indicators.note: here over means covering round, so the scrambled word encloses the other piece
hopelessly signals that the letters of pores are messed up

parts.note: a crust is a scanty portion of bread

explanation.surface: A wicked Greek pores despairingly over his scant food allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads like 'about' with 'pores over', but it is the container signal; 'hopelessly' is the anagram signal on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The robber of Greek myth stretched or lopped his guests to fit his bed, a notorious villain.

clue.text: Fantasy writer of article on Haggard book

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fantasy novelist writes an article on a book by Rider Haggard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like an adjective, but it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard, author of She.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Shea co-wrote the Illuminatus! trilogy and other imaginative novels, so he counts as an author of fantasy.

clue.text: A Graham Greene work, lettered all through?

definitions.meaning: Greene's 1938 novel of a seaside gang
the seaside sweet stick has its resort's name printed all the way through

explanation.surface: A Greene novel that seems to carry writing in every page.
explanation.walkthrough: The seaside rock of British resorts is a hard sugar stick with lettering running through its length.
explanation.definitionFit: Greene's novel is named after the striped candy sold in the Sussex resort, inscribed with the town's name inside.

clue.text: Fashion-oriented discoverer of canals?

definitions.meaning: Elsa of that surname was a famous Paris couturier
the astronomer Giovanni of that surname reported channels on Mars

explanation.surface: A stylish explorer who found waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian astronomer's word canali, meaning channels, was taken in English to mean Martian canals, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: One family name covers both the haute-couture designer and the astronomer who mapped supposed Martian waterways.

clue.text: "The devil damn thee black, thou— - — loon!" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: "The devil damn thee black, thou— - — loon!" (Macbeth)

parts.words: "The devil damn thee black, thou— - — loon!" (Macbeth)
parts.note: Macbeth curses the frightened servant as pale with fear, filling the gap in this line

explanation.surface: A line from Macbeth with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth, Act 5 Scene 3, abuses a terrified servant as white-faced with fear.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing epithet means pale-cheeked from cowardice, the insult Macbeth throws at the servant.

clue.text: Appropriate utterances of Traherne showing large conurbations supporting broken life

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath
broken means the word life is smashed and its letters reassembled

parts.note: cities are large urban areas

explanation.surface: Traherne's apt phrases show big towns propping up a shattered existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns LIFE into FELI; 'supporting' puts CITIES below it in the down entry. Thomas Traherne wrote poems of happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt, well-turned expressions are so called, and the word was also a favourite theme of the poet Traherne.

clue.text: Making more cuts reignited changes

indicators.note: changes means the letters of reignited are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making further cuts rekindled alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing a text again involves trimming it further, so another round of cuts is revision.

clue.text: Mourning became her sister

parts.note: O'Neill's play Mourning Becomes Electra recalls that Electra's sister was sacrificed at Aulis

explanation.surface: Grief suited her sister well.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill's trilogy Mourning Becomes Electra puns on 'became'; the clue asks for Electra's sister, Agamemnon's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Agamemnon's daughter, sacrificed for a fair wind to Troy, was Electra's sibling.

clue.text: Diagram is something Raphael wrote

indicators.note: what Raphael wrote is taken literally as the letters written across something Raphael

explanation.surface: A chart is something the painter Raphael drew up.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart plotting data is a standard synonym for a diagram.

clue.text: French dramatist discovers girl friend with first lover

parts.note: amie is French for a female friend

indicators.note: the first letter of lover is taken

explanation.surface: A French playwright finds a girlfriend along with her first lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Denys Amiel was a French playwright of the interwar years; 'discovers' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Denys Amiel wrote comedies for the Paris stage between the wars.

clue.text: "I— a confused and irresolute answer" (William Godwin, Caleb Williams )

definitions.text: "I— a confused and irresolute answer" (William Godwin, Caleb Williams )

parts.words: "I— a confused and irresolute answer" (William Godwin, Caleb Williams )
parts.note: a quotation from Godwin's novel with the verb missing: the speaker paused and faltered before replying

explanation.surface: A line from Godwin's novel Caleb Williams with a word to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a muddled, wavering reply follows naturally from having faltered or paused in doubt.

clue.text: Photographer rumoured to turn not exactly blue with cold

indicators.note: rumoured signals that the phrase is to be heard said aloud

parts.words: turn not exactly blue with cold
parts.note: to turn with cold is to freeze, and not exactly blue is greeny

explanation.surface: A photographer is said to go a sort of bluish shade from the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: William Friese-Greene was a British pioneer of photography and cinema; 'turn … with cold' gives freeze and 'not exactly blue' greeny, which together sound like his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Friese-Greene made early motion-picture cameras and worked as a portrait cameraman in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: English distance covered by Rousseau

parts.note: a distance

explanation.surface: Rousseau walked an English mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' looks like distance travelled, but it means treated in writing: Rousseau's treatise on education is Émile.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousseau's book on education bears the name of its imaginary pupil, so it is a subject he wrote about.

clue.text: Colette's two soldiers

indicators.note: two means the piece is used twice over

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Colette had a pair of American soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 'Colette's' stands for a work of hers: her novella about a Parisian girl trained as a courtesan.
explanation.definitionFit: Colette's 1944 novella is the work meant, the novelist's possession in that sense.

clue.text: Intricate subject for Ruth Fainlight and Eva Figes

definitions.text: Intricate subject for Ruth Fainlight and Eva Figes

parts.words: Intricate subject for Ruth Fainlight and Eva Figes
parts.note: a tangled thing, and the title of a poem by Fainlight and of a novel by Figes

explanation.surface: Two women writers tackle a complicated topic.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth Fainlight's poem and Eva Figes's 1996 novel share this title, a tangle that is intricate by nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle of tied rope is intricate, and the word titles works by both writers.

clue.text: Chastisement, say, for fratricide

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a cane is a punishment stick used for chastisement

explanation.surface: Punishment, for example, for killing one's brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Fratricide here is the person who kills a brother, not the act: Adam's son who slew Abel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis figure murdered his brother Abel, the first such killer in scripture.

clue.text: Not accepting need to observe moral law and opposed to revolutionary Minoan

definitions.text: Not accepting need to observe moral law

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: revolutionary means the letters of Minoan are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Defying morality and against a rebellious Cretan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges MINOAN to NOMIAN; 'and' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The heretical view held that faith frees Christians from obligation to the moral code.

clue.text: Beach produced it, and it was on the sea

definitions.text: Beach produced it, and it was on the sea

parts.words: Beach produced it, and it was on the sea
parts.note: Edward L. Beach wrote the submarine novel ... on the Sea; the beach also makes sand

explanation.surface: Something churned out by a beach that drifted over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Beach is the American naval novelist Edward L. Beach, whose book Dust on the Sea supplies the answer and its context.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine powdery particles, which a sandy shore throws up, form the first word of Beach's naval novel title.

clue.text: Redirect talks giver to present Swedish writer

indicators.note: to redirect the words talks giver is to send their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Redirect a speaker to present a Swedish author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to present' is a link. Pär Lagerkvist won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel laureate wrote Barabbas and was a Swedish novelist and poet.
